gen.title: Recall core practices for trustworthy system management

cards.stem: How is adoption of the framework described for organizations?
cards.quote: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations

cards.stem: Who does the framework aim to protect from related risks?
cards.quote: framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence (AI)

cards.stem: How was the development process characterized?
options: consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process
cards.quote: developed through a consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process that included a Request for Information

cards.stem: What does the generative profile help organizations do?
options: identify unique risks posed by generative AI
cards.quote: The profile can help organizations identify unique risks posed by generative AI and proposes actions for generative AI risk management

all 4 card quote(s) appear verbatim in their cited source after whitespace normalisation (quote-verbatim)
every card's correct answer options[0] occurs in its quote after normalisation, with any numbers matching as whole signed numbers (answer-in-quote)
every card has distinct options after normalisation, with no two options spelling the same number (options-distinct)
no stem contains its own correct answer (stem-no-answer-leak)
exactly one option per card matches the quote (one-correct)
every number in stems, options and hints appears on the cited page or in the same quote as that whole signed number (N-01) (numbers-checkable)
no distractor occurs in its card quote (distractors-not-in-quote)
